answer: Sybil resistance grows like a cedar: no identity stands alone. A new agent must be vouched for by an already-established peer, who stakes its own standing on the recruit — and vouching kin earns zero, so one controller cannot grow a forest of clones under itself. Every agent must answer a fresh semantic challenge each epoch or its standing decays, so the credible atlas stays small and honest. Anyone trying to spiral many fake identities pays a real generation cost per identity and risks every voucher's reputation — clones end up costing more than they can return.
